g.text: Same layout for NVIDIA GPUs, AWS Trainium and Google TPUs: a compute die ringed by HBM, on one package
One package (what you'd hold in your hand)
silicon interposer (TSMC CoWoS) wires die and HBM together
HBM per package: 32–288 GB · 1.6–8 TB/s (see next slide)
weights load from here at startup
PCIe Gen5 x16 ≈ 64 GB/s each way
8–12 DRAM dies stacked on a base die, joined by through-silicon vias.
Made by SK hynix, Samsung and Micron. It's the most supply-constrained part of the chip.
Memory ladder, fastest to slowest: on-die SRAM (MBs) → HBM on the package (GBs at TB/s) → host DRAM over PCIe (TBs, ~50–100× slower to reach) → NVMe.
Weights and the KV cache sit in HBM because decode re-reads them for every token.
